analysis.summary: An Amazon cargo plane overran a runway at Miami International Airport, struck several vehicles, and killed at least five people while injuring five more. The Boeing 767 aircraft, which had flown from Puerto Rico, caught fire after the runway excursion. Investigations by U.S. aviation authorities are underway as the airport operates with reduced runway capacity.

context.significance: Runway excursions — where aircraft leave the prepared runway surface — are one of the most consistently identified risk categories in global aviation safety reports, yet this incident is exceptional in that fatalities appear to have occurred primarily in vehicles on or near the runway, exposing the lethal danger posed to airport ground workers and motorists. The crash also draws attention to the rapid expansion of e-commerce air freight operations, where contracted carriers operate under commercial pressures and oversight frameworks that can differ significantly from major passenger airlines. If the investigation points to crew fatigue, maintenance failures, or inadequate runway safety areas, it will intensify debate about regulatory standards governing the cargo aviation sector.
